newsitem.title: USA: N.C. trestle collapses in Danny floodwaters.
newsitem.headline: N.C. trestle collapses in Danny floodwaters.

text.p: A railroad trestle over a creek collapsed Wednesday, sending five rail cars plunging into floodwaters caused by heavy rain from the remnants of Hurricane Danny, authorities said.

A woman drowned when her car was stranded in another rain-swollen creek as residents struggled to cope with rising floodwaters from up to six inches of rain. Emergency crews evacuated residents from apartment complexes and homes in several areas of the city.
A flash flood watch was in effect for the Charlotte region as two storm systems converged on the city from the south and west. Forecasters predicted as much as six more inches of rain could fall.
Floodwaters in Little Sugar Creek collapsed the rail trestle's supports, sending five CSX Corp railcars into the water, authorities said. Many of the train's cars did not go into the water.
The crew scrambled to safety and fuel washed into the creek but posed no danger, officials said.

"The creek's waters were moving so fast that the oil was swept along too quickly for it to be dangerous," Julie Hill, the city's corporate communications director, said from the emergency operations centre.

Barbara White Freeman, 59, of Gastonia, North Carolina, drowned in Stewart Creek when her car was stranded in flood waters, authorities said. A 5-year-old girl was missing in another flood-related incident.

Crews from the city's emergency operations centre were checking for structural damage to roads, bridges and buildings. Residents were urged to leave work early for home to avoid getting caught floodwaters.
Hurricane Danny slogged ashore along the Gulf Coast this week, dumping heavy rain on parts of Louisiana, Alabama and the Florida panhandle.
